newsitem.title: FRANCE: Defence official resigns, savages French system.
newsitem.headline: Defence official resigns, savages French system.

text.p: A senior French defence official who resigned this month savaged the government on Wednesday, saying reforms vital to overhaul a bloated system had misfired.
"Making the state worthy of being understood is the main problem of our country," said Jean Picq, who had been entrusted with overseeing a defence review by conservative Prime Minister Alain Juppe.

Picq, the head of the General Secretariat of National Defence (SGDN), told the daily Les Echos he resigned after government efforts to privatise defence electronics giant Thomson SA ran off the rails this month.
"Interministerial work aimed at enlightening those in charge, clarifying risks, suggesting necessary precautions, were not always well used," he said.
He said reforms of the state had misfired because no one was willing to tackle underlying problems.
Among recommendations, he said the number of government ministers should be sharply reduced to 15 and national officials should be barred from holding other posts.

"Can you imagine a corporate boss who was also mayor of a major city or of a regional council?" he asked in a barely veiled attack on Juppe, mayor of the southwest city of Bordeaux and head of the Gaullist Rally for the Republic (RPR) party.
